title: 5T OTA
description: The five-transistor OTA, biased from the TAIL NODE and entered from the COMMON MODE. Internally the tail node is the one free bias variable: the pair's source sits at $V_{tail}$, so its body bias is $V_{tail}$, its drain-source voltage is $V_{out} - V_{tail}$, and every device is read straight out of the table with nothing iterated. Externally the designer types the common mode the application presents: $CM_{in} = V_{tail} + V_{GS}$ rises monotonically with the tail node, so the engine brackets $V_{tail}$ and bisects until the produced common mode equals $CM_{dc}$ — an inversion that cannot overshoot and owes nothing to a starting guess. Sweep $CM_{dc}$ to trace the common-mode axis. Gain falls as the common mode rises, because lifting the tail node squeezes the pair's own $v_{ds}$ — and it collapses well before the pair leaves saturation, which is why the gain rule, not a saturation edge, sets the usable ceiling.

params.name: vn_target
params.note: input-referred thermal density budget, set above the 28 nV/rtHz floor measured on a sky130 tt realization of this OTA rather than above the gamma-model row (21.5 nV/rtHz at the default 20 uA and gm/ID split). Clearing only the model is how a spec looks closable and is not; tighten this and the sweep shows what the noise really costs

params.name: vos_target
params.note: input offset budget, 1 sigma. Half-micron devices at 20 uA are SMALL (about 2 um x 0.5 um here), so the generic Pelgrom coefficient puts the spread near 8 mV — offset is the 5T's area tax, and shrinking this budget is what forces bigger devices

params.name: CM_lo
params.note: input CM range the application presents, low edge. The cm-lo edge re-evaluates the whole sheet here, so this claim is CHECKED at every evaluation, on the design this run produced — the sweep shows the widest range that would close (0.95-1.39 V on sky130 tt at the shipped choices). The edge checks the ENDPOINT; the interior is the sweep's to show

params.name: CM_hi
params.note: input CM range the application presents, high edge — its ENDPOINT checked by the cm-hi edge the same way

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: output DC level; sets the mirror output device's vds and the top of the pair's own vds

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the tail node — the design's one free bias variable, solved rather than set: the engine bisects between min and max (the BRACKET, not slider bounds) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc. It fixes the pair's body bias and drain-source voltage in one stroke; the shown value is where it landed. Both bracket ends must size: lowering V_out_dc below the max here leaves the pair no drain-source voltage at the high end, and the pin will say so

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion: sets gm per current, noise, and the CM-low edge

params.name: gm_id_ld
params.note: mirror-load inversion: lower gm/ID adds less noise and offset (both scale with the load's gm)

params.name: gm_id_tail
params.note: tail inversion: higher V* costs CM-low headroom

params.name: ld_sign
params.note: vds sign convention of the load table: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

doc.title: Mirror-load device
doc.description: One side of the mirror load at half the tail current. Its bias never moves with the input common mode — the output node and the supply set it — so its $g_{ds}$ and its diode drop are fixed once the output level is chosen.

params.name: vds_l
params.note: output-side vds, signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: Input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current, sized at the OUTPUT-side drain — the pair devices share a gate drive and a source but not a drain, and it is the output-side one whose $g_{ds}$ loads the gain. Both of its bias coordinates come from the tail node directly: the source sits at $V_{tail}$, so that is its body bias, and its drain-source voltage is what is left between the output level and that source.

doc.title: Tail current source
doc.description: The tail device carrying the full bias current, with the tail node as its drain-source voltage. It leaves saturation when $V_{tail}$ falls below its own $V_{dsat}$, which is what sets the low end of the usable common-mode range.

rows.name: CM_in
rows.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting. It rises monotonically with the tail node — which is why the pin that places the tail node from $CM_{dc}$ is a well-posed bisection

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: the resistance this OTA presents at its output — the two output-node conductances in parallel, both read at $V_{out,dc}$. The gain below assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this row is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

rows.name: Av
rows.note: half-circuit differential gain into the two output conductances, both read at the OUTPUT node $V_{out,dc}$ — the drain that actually loads the gain. Raising the tail node squeezes the pair's $v_{ds}$, so gain falls as the common mode rises

rows.name: f_pole
rows.note: estimate: the mirror-node pole, the load's $g_m$ over both mirror gates' $C_{GG}$; the 5T's second pole. Read at the output-side bias — the diode side's own $g_m$ differs only by the shallow $g_m(v_{ds})$ slope, a few percent

rows.name: PM
rows.note: estimate: phase margin left after the mirror node. That node is a pole-ZERO DOUBLET, not a lone pole — only half the signal takes the mirror path, putting a zero at twice the pole — so it costs far less phase than $f_{pole}$ alone suggests

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: both pair devices and both mirror devices contribute, each at its own density: 2*(vn_pair^2 + vn_ld^2*(gm_ld/gm_in)^2) (simulation-verified two-sided total)

rows.name: vos
rows.expr: sqrt(pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, in__W, L_in, gm_id_in)^2 + (pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, ld__W, L_ld, gm_id_ld)*ld__gm/in__gm)^2)
rows.note: input-pair offset plus the mirror pair's offset referred by the gm ratio

rows.name: tail_headroom
rows.note: how far the tail node sits above the tail device's saturation edge — exact here, because the tail node is the variable rather than something inferred from a common mode

rows.name: cgg_in
rows.note: estimate: the capacitance one input terminal presents — the gate capacitance of a single input device. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No rule reads it

rows.name: I_q
rows.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — the tail current is the whole of it, because the mirror load carries that same current down from the supply. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no rule reads it

rules.note: estimate: margin left at crossover once the mirror doublet is paid for; advisory, since an open-loop OTA needs none of it and sim owns the real stability
computed from the gamma-model floor; this table carries no measured noise; the simulator owns noise sign-off
below this the tail source drops out of saturation and the bias current collapses; this is the mechanism behind the low end of the common-mode range
the common mode this bias produces has to sit inside the range the application presents
paired with cm-not-below. Sweep $CM_{dc}$ to see the whole span that closes — that span, not a saturation formula, is the common-mode range this design really supports

rules.justification: the pair's two drains sit at different levels — one a diode drop below the supply, the other at the output — and which is lower depends on V_out_dc, so this watches whichever it is. Gain collapses well before this trips, so treat it as a floor rather than as the usable ceiling
rules.note: trips when the tail node is pushed so high the pair runs out of drain-source voltage — lower V_tail, or spend less diode drop (lower gm_id_ld)

edges.name: cm-lo
edges.note: the claimed low edge, checked exactly: the whole sheet re-evaluates at CM_dc = CM_lo on the design this run produced — its own tail-node solve from the full bracket, every device held at the geometry it was sized to — and every hard rule must hold there. Replaces the linearized reach estimate this sheet used to carry

edges.name: cm-hi
edges.note: the claimed high edge, checked the same way. The edges check the ENDPOINTS; the interior is monotone for the saturation mechanisms here, and the CM_dc sweep remains the authority on the full landscape
